subject: Dedicated capacity: single-tenant isolation & pricing for Acme Cloud Analytics

Subject: Dedicated capacity: single-tenant isolation & pricing for Acme Cloud Analytics

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. Acme is evaluating a Dedicated deployment in a single-tenant / isolated GPU pool for our analytics workloads. Two immediate asks from procurement and security:

1) A line-item price breakdown for the Dedicated SKU with the single-tenant isolation premium (items we need separated: base reserved commit, isolation premium, KMS integration, audit-log retention, and any per-token or per-GB egress charges).
2) Throughput guarantees and an example sizing for a 500 concurrent session workload with average 1024-token generation per session (we care about P95 latency and sustained throughput).
3) Compliance evidence (SOC2 excerpt and an outline of how KMS/HSM is integrated).

We also expect to discuss a multi-year commit; please show comparator pricing for 12/24/36 month reserved commits.

Please send a formal proposal and any attachments we can circulate with procurement/security.

-Jordan

Hi Jordan — great talking yesterday. Attached is a concise pricing proposal that separates the items you requested and shows commit tiers for 12/24/36 months. Highlights up front:

- Base reserved commit: quoted as $50k/mo per 8xA100-equivalent pool for the baseline throughput profile.
- Single-tenant isolation surcharge: +22% on base for an isolated GPU pool with dedicated networking and tenant-specific orchestration.
- Compliance add-ons: KMS integration (customer-managed keys) + audit-log retention (90/365 day options) — line items included.
- Throughput guarantees: P95 latency SLO of 250ms for 1024-token responses under the proposed 500-concurrent-session sizing when disk-backed KV cache is enabled; burst policies and autoscale described.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Proposal_ACME_v1.pdf (contains tables and sample math).

If you like, Marcus Lin (cc'd) can follow up with a quick capacity worksheet mapping your qps and token distributions to pool counts. Happy to schedule a follow-up to walk the deck.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: single-tenant isolation & pricing for Acme Cloud Analytics

Jordan / Samira — digging into the sizing question so you have concrete numbers. Key technical notes:

- We model a 500 concurrent sessions workload as ~7.5M tokens/minute sustained with spikes to ~12M tokens/min. For that profile, the recommended starting configuration is 3 x 8xA100-equivalent pools (reserved) with one small warm standby pool for bursts.
- With KV prefix caching and sequence-length-aware batching, the expected token cost is reduced ~18% over naive per-token serving; we account for that in the pricing doc.
- P95 latency target of 250ms assumes our continuous batching window at 5ms and a max-batch-size cap tuned for low-latency workloads; we include a fallback policy to a lower-cost model (quantized) if node utilization > 85% to preserve availability.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS or HSM by integration) — key wrap and per-tenant key usage audit is logged to the private control plane and exported to your SIEM via secure syslog/S3. SOC2 excerpts attached.

I've attached a quick capacity worksheet and a short runbook for failover and autoscale. Happy to run a short bench session with a sample payload if you want to validate the numbers before procurement signs off.

Attachments: capacity_worksheet_acme_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SOC2-Attestation-Excerpt.pdf

- Marcus

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: single-tenant isolation & pricing for Acme Cloud Analytics

Kimberly, Marcus — thanks for the fast turnaround and the worksheet. We've reviewed the proposal internally and have two items from procurement/security before we can move to legal:

1) The single-tenant isolation surcharge at 22% is higher than we anticipated. Comparable vendors we're evaluating are showing premiums in the 12-15% range for fully isolated pools. Is there flexibility on that surcharge with a 36-month committed contract?
2) We'd like the 90-day audit-log retention (included) to be extended to 365 days for security reasons — please quote incremental cost for 365-day retention and confirm whether the logs can be exported to our S3 with encryption retained under our KMS.

I've attached procurement's redlines to the pricing deck — some commercial language and requested credit terms.

-Jordan

Attachments: ACME_Procurement_Redlines_20260728.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <secops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: single-tenant isolation & pricing for Acme Cloud Analytics

Jordan — appreciate the clear ask and the redlines. Quick answer summary and a final commercial option we can provisionally offer: 

- Isolation surcharge: we can move from 22% -> 16% for a 36-month reserved commit at the same pool sizing (three 8xA100-equivalent pools). To make that concession, we require a 6% one-time onboarding credit applied against month 1-3 invoices OR a single up-front onboarding fee waiver (your choice).
- 365-day audit-log retention: supported. Incremental cost is a flat $4,500/mo for the additional storage and longer-term immutable retention controls; logs can be exported to your S3 bucket with encryption preserved under your customer-managed KMS.
- KMS integration: confirmed — we will provide per-key usage logs, and Marcus will prepare the integration checklist for your security team.

If you accept the 36-month commit + the onboarding-credit condition, I will route the proposal to Legal with the commercial mark we discussed and provide a DocuSign package. Logan (cc'd, Sales Manager) is included to approve the concession.

Next steps: please confirm which onboarding option you prefer and whether the 36-month term works for your CFO/procurement. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize the commercial terms.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
